questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

A household which spends all of its income on bananas and apples makes the following purchases. price per fruit unit ($) bananas 2.50 apples 1.00 The household derives twice as much utility from the last unit of bananas consumed as from the last unit of apples consumed. What should the household do to maximise utility from the consumption of these fruits? consumption consumption of bananas of apples

options.D: no change increase

questions.questionText: The curve JK in the diagram is a consumer’s initial budget line. G J good Y O H K good X Which combination could cause the budget line to shift to GH? price of consumer’s good X money income

options.D: decrease increase

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a perfectly competitive firm’s average product of labour (APL) and marginal product of labour (MPL) curves. J K wage, labour product M L APL MPL O number of workers employed The market price of the firm’s product is $1. Which segment of the curves represents the firm’s demand for labour curve?

options.A: OJ B JK C KL D KM

questions.questionText: The table shows the main characteristics of employment in two alternative occupations. occupation X occupation Y average annual wage $80000 $100000 number of weeks annual leave 10 weeks 5 weeks average length of working week 44 hours 48 hours job security low high length of training course to obtain job qualification 2 years 1 year What can definitely be deduced from the table?

options.A: Occupation Y has greater non-financial advantages than occupation X.
options.B: There will be more competition for places on training courses to enter occupation X than occupation Y.
options.C: Those who choose occupation X attach more importance to leisure activities than those who choose occupation Y.
options.D: Those who choose occupation Y attach greater importance to job security than those who choose occupation X.

questions.questionText: A trade union seeks to increase the wages a firm pays to its workers while at the same time preserving jobs. What will strengthen the union’s negotiating position?

options.A: Capital and labour are close substitutes.
options.B: The demand for the good produced by the firm is price elastic.
options.C: The supply of labour to the firm is perfectly elastic.
options.D: The trade union operates in a monopsonistic labour market.

questions.questionText: When a firm increases all its inputs by 300%, its output increases by 400%. What does this illustrate?

options.D: the law of variable proportions

questions.questionText: The average variable costs of a firm are constant over the relevant range of output. Assuming that fixed costs are incurred, which curve on the diagram could be the firm’s average total cost curve over this range? A B costs C D O output
Which is an example of an external diseconomy?

options.A: difficulties in coordinating activities in a large organisation
options.B: difficulties in motivating workers in a large organisation
options.C: higher transport costs as a firm’s market expands
options.D: increased traffic congestion as industries expand

questions.questionText: What makes it easier for a small firm to compete against large firms in the same industry?

options.A: The nature of the industry’s product is highly standardised.
options.B: The product specification demanded by each customer is different.
options.C: There are significant barriers facing potential new entrants.
options.D: Transport costs are low relative to the value of the product.

options.A: w + v B w + z C w – v D w only

options.D: MC
options.A: R O MR number of copies

LRAC LRMC cost, revenue AR MR O output Which statements correctly describe the performance of this firm? the firm is the firm is fully operating with exploiting available excess capacity economies of scale

options.D: yes no

questions.questionText: In the diagram, D is the demand curve for cigarettes, S is the supply curve and MSC is the marginal social cost curve. MSC S1 S price P D O Q quantity The introduction of a specific tax on cigarettes causes the supply curve to shift to S1. What are likely to be the impacts of the tax on economic efficiency and the tax system? economic efficiency tax system

options.D: worsens more regressive

questions.questionText: Which combination of policy changes is most likely to redistribute income from the richest households to the poorest households in an economy? means-tested universal excise duties benefits benefits

options.D: increase decrease decrease

questions.questionText: In order to reduce milk production, all producers are given a quota which limits the amount of milk each producer is allowed to produce. Initially, the quotas cannot be traded. What will be the effect on the total volume of milk production and on the overall profits of milk producers if they are allowed to trade the quotas among themselves? effect on effect on total volume profits

options.D: unchanged decrease

questions.questionText: During a year, a country’s national income in money terms increased by 5%, prices increased by 4% and the total population increased by 2%. What was the approximate change in real income per head?

options.D: an increase of 2%

questions.questionText: Which represents an injection into an economy’s circular flow of income?

options.D: the retained profits of private companies

questions.questionText: In a closed economy with no government sector, investment is increased by $100million and real income increases by $500million. What is the marginal propensity to consume?
The income velocity of circulation is equal to 2.0. If the rate of growth of the money supply is 8% and the average price level increases by 4%, what will be the change in real output (transactions)?

The diagram shows the demand curves and supply curves of loanable funds. The market is in equilibrium at point X. What would be the new equilibrium point if there were an increase in business confidence and a reduction in the propensity to save? S

options.D: 2 B S

questions.questionText: What will be most likely to decrease a country’s national output in the short-run but to increase its potential for long-run growth?

options.A: a decrease in the level of import tariffs
options.B: a decrease in the rate of immigration
options.C: an increase in female participation in the labour force
options.D: an increase in the money supply

questions.questionText: Which change would best indicate that a country has experienced economic development?

options.A: an appreciation in the country’s currency
options.B: an improvement in the average citizen’s quality of life
options.C: an improvement in the country’s trade balance
options.D: an increase in the country’s real GDP

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the relationship between the rate of inflation and the rate of unemployment. F J inflation rate G K O unemployment rate What would cause the curve FG to shift to JK?

options.B: a lower expected rate of inflation
options.D: a rise in the level of employment

questions.questionText: What is the best measure of the economic cost of an increase in unemployment?

options.A: the additional social security benefits paid plus the loss of tax revenue from newly unemployed workers
options.C: the money value of the additional social security benefits paid
options.D: the output the unemployed workers could have produced

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the actual output and expected output of an economy. expected output output actual output O time What would help to reduce the divergence of actual output from expected output?

options.D: stable interest rates

questions.questionText: In an economy with a fixed exchange rate, which combination of policies is likely to be most effective at tackling both a growing current account deficit on the balance of payments and rising inflationary pressure?

options.A: a budget deficit and higher interest rates
options.B: a budget deficit and lower interest rates
options.C: a budget surplus and higher interest rates
options.D: a budget surplus and lower interest rates

questions.questionText: The table gives details of a government’s budget over two years. 2012/13 2013/14 (US$ millions) (US$ millions) government revenue 2630000 3730000 government spending 3000300 3770000 What happened to government finances between 2012/13 and 2013/14?

options.D: The national debt rose.

questions.questionText: In an open economy, what is most likely to cause the money supply to fall?

options.B: an increase in the ratio of cash reserves to total deposits in the commercial banking sector
options.C: central bank bond purchases from the non-bank private sector
options.D: government borrowing from the commercial banking sector

questions.questionText: A government responds to a fall in national income by increasing its spending. It finances the increased spending by issuing bonds to the non-bank private sector. What is likely to be one of the consequences of this policy?

options.A: a crowding out of private investment
options.B: a decreased balance of trade deficit
options.C: a reduction in the money supply
